clue.text: State capital's fortune gained with effort from east

parts.note: fortune here means luck, good or bad chance

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to have won something is to have gained it by striving

explanation.surface: A state capital is said to have made its money through hard work coming from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' asks for a right-to-left reading in an across entry. The city is the capital of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is the capital city of the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh; the possessive 's is absorbed as 'is'.

clue.text: Inaugurate church with articles in Le Figaro

parts.note: la is a French definite article, as one would see in the newspaper Le Figaro
un is the French indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church is opened with pieces in a French newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Figaro is a French daily, so its articles are French ones: LA and UN.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a venture is to set it going formally, to inaugurate it.

clue.text: Warning giving rise to wariness

definitions.meaning: an official warning or admonition, as a referee or police officer gives
carefulness, prudence in the face of risk

explanation.surface: A warning makes one more careful.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word means both a formal warning and the quality of carefulness.

clue.text: Revolutionary rule again producing intermittent pain

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radical rule imposed once more causes recurring pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is intense pain along a nerve, typically coming in sharp intermittent bouts.

clue.text: Kindly-intentioned source introducing import

indicators.note: the source word comes first, introducing the next piece

parts.note: a well is a source of water
import means significance, meaning

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted supplier brings in foreign goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-meaning has good intentions, so is kindly-intentioned.

clue.text: Converts the smugly virtuous may claim to have?

definitions.text: Converts the smugly virtuous may claim to have?

parts.words: Converts the smugly virtuous may claim to have?
parts.note: read as a phrase split in two, the smug boast is of having no failings or bad habits at all; read whole, the word means beginners or new converts

explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers to a religious order or faith, recent converts, are called by this word for beginners.

clue.text: Tug almost capsized? Not at all

indicators.note: in a down clue capsized means turned upside down, read from bottom to top
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to yank is to tug sharply

explanation.surface: A tugboat has nearly overturned, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims YANK to YAN; 'capsized' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old word for no, a flat refusal or denial, as in not at all.

clue.text: Head of venerable university holding a dance

indicators.note: the letters before hold the article inside
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics, a university college

explanation.surface: The head of an old university holds a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside V plus LSE, the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Valse is the French word for waltz, used in English for the dance.

clue.text: Sort of surgery 2 put on current account?

parts.note: the solution to 2 down can mean an amusing person, a card
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Surgery of some kind is carried out on someone's current account.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 2 down (a warning) can also mean a comic, a card. 'put on' places CARD first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac surgery is surgery on the heart, so cardiac names a sort of surgery.

clue.text: Case one may find when walking along the Strand?

definitions.text: Case one may find when walking along the Strand?

parts.words: Case one may find when walking along the Strand?
parts.note: the Strand looks like the London street, but a strand is a beach, where one finds shell casings of marine creatures

explanation.definitionFit: A seashell is the hard protective case of a sea creature, found on beaches.

clue.text: Rarely in France a posh girl takes in university

parts.note: the French indefinite article is un
U is the old label for upper-class usage, so posh

indicators.note: the girl's name swallows the next piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Apparently, a smart young woman in France seldom goes to college.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh is the old 'U and non-U' label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusually and rarely are both adverbs meaning not often or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Grub produced in granular varieties

indicators.note: the letters are produced from within the run of the words granular varieties

explanation.surface: A grub turns up in various kinds of granular material.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature grub stage of an insect.

clue.text: Outstanding feature by a friend or companion

parts.note: the chin sticks out of the face, a feature that literally stands out

explanation.surface: A notable characteristic of a friend or companion is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA means a mate from Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: China, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate for mate, is British slang for a friend.

clue.text: Capuchins are so, even without extremes of energy

definitions.text: Capuchins are so, even without extremes of energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the friarly word goes round the next letters

parts.note: Capuchins are Franciscan friars, so they are like monks

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word energy are taken

explanation.surface: Capuchin friars behave in a cheeky, simian way even when they have no energy left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. The whole clue is the definition too, since capuchins are also a kind of monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Capuchin monkeys are naturally ape-like, and the friars sharing their name are monkish, so both readings describe them.

clue.text: Not a single country's accepting Michigan's proposals

indicators.note: the phrase takes in the state abbreviation

parts.note: not a single country is no nations, the 's read as is
MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan

explanation.surface: No nation will go along with Michigan's suggestions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'country's' as possessive; it is really 'country is', part of a phrase about no country at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominations are names put forward, which are proposals of candidates.

clue.text: Like East Grinstead in relation to its tea gardens

definitions.text: Like East Grinstead in relation to its tea gardens

parts.words: Like East Grinstead in relation to its tea gardens
parts.note: the letters of the town name can be rearranged to spell the phrase tea gardens, so the town name is a rearrangement of that phrase

explanation.walkthrough: EAST GRINSTEAD is a town in West Sussex; its letters can be rearranged to spell 'tea gardens' and more besides.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Lean actor protecting extremely unusual source of timber

indicators.note: the outer pieces guard the inner letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to tip is to lean or tilt

indicators.note: the extreme letters of unusual, its first and last, are taken

parts.note: Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated actor-manager

explanation.surface: A thin actor shelters an exceptionally strange supply of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean actor' suggests a skinny performer, but 'Lean' is a verb, tilt, and the actor is the Edwardian stage star Beerbohm Tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip tree is a large North American tree valued for its timber, so a source of wood.

clue.text: Chapel? I'll wager the man's a lawyer!

parts.note: to bet is to wager
the man's is he's, the man is
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone bets that the fellow is an attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethesda is a common name for Welsh nonconformist chapels, after the biblical pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a name used for a nonconformist chapel, especially in Wales, so stands for one.

clue.text: Old European coin, one catalogued by English teacher

parts.note: the ducat was a gold coin used across Europe in past centuries
I is the Roman numeral for one
something catalogued is on a list

explanation.surface: An English teacher catalogues an antique European coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one catalogued' as ON A LIST after I; 'by English' puts E alongside, at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An educationalist is a specialist in teaching and education, so a teacher in a broad sense.

clue.text: Disconcert peace promoters, at no time raising resistance

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, promotes peace

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letter higher in the word

parts.note: at no time means never

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers are rattled, never strengthening their opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising resistance' moves R, the symbol for electrical resistance, up NEVER to make NERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to make them lose their composure, to disconcert them.

clue.text: Newspaper's pension provision Star's regular feature

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper; the 's is kept
a pension pot is a fund saved for retirement

explanation.surface: A tabloid's pension plan is a regular item in a star's column.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper; 'Star' is also a tabloid name, but here it means the sun itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunspots are dark patches regularly seen on the surface of the sun, a star.

clue.text: Where Clementine's father dwelt, unknown to break the law

indicators.note: the unknown letter breaks into the law word, splitting it

parts.note: canon means a law or rule, especially church law
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Clementine's dad lived there, without knowing he was breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: In the song 'Oh My Darling, Clementine', her miner father dwelt 'in a cavern, in a canyon'. 'to break' puts Y inside CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk song places Clementine's father, a forty-niner miner, living in a canyon.

clue.text: With which one may belatedly appreciate farm-worker's vision

definitions.text: With which one may belatedly appreciate

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer; the possessive s doubles as the start of the next word
vision means sight

explanation.surface: A farm labourer's eyesight lets them understand things only too late.
explanation.walkthrough: A hind is an old British term for a farm worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindsight is understanding an event only after it has happened, so it lets one appreciate things belatedly.

clue.text: Laxative an old queen's given up

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Queen Anne was an English queen of the early 1700s; the 's is kept

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch has surrendered her purgative.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna, made from cassia plant pods, is a well-known herbal laxative.

clue.text: Old man going around with a herbivorous mammal

indicators.note: the father word goes round the link word, enclosing it

parts.note: old man is slang for father, pa
with can mean and

explanation.surface: An elderly man walks about with a plant-eating animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word joining the man to the mammal, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a mammal living almost entirely on bamboo, so a plant eater.

clue.text: Male parent's name for seductive singer

parts.note: a sire is a male parent, especially of an animal; the 's is read as has

explanation.surface: A father's name for an alluring vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors to their doom with enchanting song.

clue.text: Great harpy originally restricting start of one's life

indicators.note: the big word confines the next letter within it

parts.note: great means big

indicators.note: the first letter of the word one's is taken
originally means arranged in an original, novel way, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A huge mythical harpy first confined a person's early days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like it means 'at first', pointing to an initial letter; here it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is a written account of someone's life story, a biography.

clue.text: Worker possibly lacking the ultimate in muscular power

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: beef is slang for muscle or brawn

explanation.surface: A labourer might be short of the final bit of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is the bee that does the colony's labour; 'possibly' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees do the hive's labour, so a bee is an example of a worker.

clue.text: Typical welcome given to current fad

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
the current craze is all the rage

explanation.surface: A welcome that goes along with the latest craze is nothing unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Average and typical both describe what is normal or usual.

clue.text: Soften up very little, covered by gun

indicators.note: the small word is wrapped inside the gun

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
wee is Scottish for small or very little

explanation.surface: To win someone over, offer a tiny gesture backed up by a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten was a cheap British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone up is to soften them, making them more agreeable before a request.
